narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and how long you have lived at your current residence. 

Your requested loan amount of 2,039 DM was noticeably lower than the average amount approved applicants ask for (about 3,020 DM). This smaller request worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward approval. However, two other important details worked against you. Your checking account currently holds between 0 and 200 DM, a situation that is less common among approved applicants and increased your risk score. In addition, having lived at your present address for only one year is shorter than the typical approved applicant, and this also nudged the model toward viewing you as higher risk.

Taken together, the negative influence from your checking account status and short time at your current residence outweighed the positive effect of the smaller loan amount, leading to the denial.

You should focus on building a stronger checking account balance and consider waiting until you have lived at your current address longer before reapplying. Improving these two areas would likely improve your chances on a future application. (218 words)
